excerpt:
Given('the catalog holds two products')(() => Effect.void),
When('the shopper searches for lamps')('found', () => Shop.search('lamps')),
why: The Given claims stored products and builds none.

excerpt:
Given('the catalog holds two products')(() => Effect.void),
When('the shopper searches')('found', () => Shop.search('lamps').pipe(Effect.provide(catalogWith(products)))),
why: The precondition is injected by the When, so the Given is decoration.

excerpt: When('the shopper searches')('found', () => Shop.search('lamps').pipe(Effect.provide(Layer.succeed(Catalog, Catalog.of({ find: () => Effect.succeed([lamp]) }))))),
why: A first-party service is replaced by a hand-built object with no contract suite; the scenario proves the stub.

excerpt:
Feature('the price index').withScenarioLayer(Layer.empty).body(({ scenario }) => scenario('a lamp is indexed', Gherkin.Do.pipe(
  Given('a lamp priced at 40')(() => Effect.void),
  When('the index is built')('index', () => Effect.sync(() => priceIndexOf(files))),
why: A pure function behind a Feature title: no world, no consumer entry.

excerpt: When('the order total is computed')('total', () => Effect.sync(() => totalOf(lines))),
why: totalOf is an internal helper the consumer never calls.

excerpt: Then('the provider receives a POST')(({}, expect) => expect(provider.received[0].method).toBe('POST')),
why: Reads a stand-in's wire record, not what our caller observes.

excerpt: When('the settings layer is built')('settings', () => Effect.provide(ShopConfig, ShopConfig.layer)),
why: Builds a layer directly; it is a unit test of configuration.

excerpt:
Given('the catalog holds a lamp')(() => Shop.addProduct(lamp)),
When('the shopper searches for lamps')('found', () => Shop.search('lamps')),
Then('the lamp is listed')(({ found }, expect) => expect(found.map((p) => p.name)).toEqual(['lamp'])),
why: State is built through the system's own operation, the When is the consumer's entry, the Then reads its result.

excerpt:
Given('no products have been added')(() => Effect.void),
When('the shopper searches for lamps')('found', () => Shop.search('lamps')),
Then('nothing is listed')(({ found }, expect) => expect(found).toEqual([])),
why: Edge case: the Given claims emptiness and the real world starts empty, so a no-op body is truthful.

excerpt:
pairwiseFor([['fake', CatalogFake.layer], ['real', CatalogPostgres.layer]], ({ scenario }) => scenario('a stored product is found', Gherkin.Do.pipe(
  Given('a stored lamp')(() => Catalog.use((c) => c.add(lamp))),
  When('the lamp is looked up')('found', () => Catalog.use((c) => c.find('lamp'))),
why: A port fake that runs in its contract suite beside the real adapter passes question 4.

excerpt:
Given('a price list with a lamp at 40')('list', () => Effect.succeed(PriceList.make([lamp]))),
When('the caller asks for the lamp price')('price', ({ list }) => Pricing.priceOf(list, 'lamp')),
why: In a library package the published operation (Pricing.priceOf) is the consumer's entry; the Given binds the value it claims.

excerpt:
Feature('Searching the catalog')
  When('the shopper searches')('found', () => Shop.search('lamps').pipe(Effect.provide(Layer.succeed(Catalog, { find: () => Effect.succeed([lamp]) } as never)))),
why: A consumer-language title over a stubbed body: judged by the body, not the title.
